articles.title: Hong Kong's Huanggang Port Border Zone Opens Under Local Law
articles.summary: A major milestone for cross-border travel happened at midnight on August 1, 2026, when the Hong Kong side of the Huanggang Port border zone officially began operating under Hong Kong law. The Hong Kong government had previously worked with the Shenzhen municipal government to sign a cooperation agreement for the arrangement. Security Secretary Tang Ping-keung was present to mark the occasion. The new setup means that travellers crossing between Hong Kong and Shenzhen at this checkpoint will now experience smoother and more consistent border procedures managed by Hong Kong authorities. Officials hope this will help attract more visitors and boost connections between the two cities.

lv1: Which border crossing point started operating under Hong Kong law on August 1, 2026? (哪個口岸在2026年8月1日起由香港法律管轄？)
Which two cities are connected by the Huanggang Port crossing? (皇崗口岸連接哪兩個城市？)
lv2: Why do you think it is important for both Hong Kong and Shenzhen to sign a cooperation agreement before the border zone could be managed by Hong Kong? (你認為為何香港和深圳在口岸由香港管轄前，需要簽署合作安排？)
How might having the Hong Kong side of Huanggang Port under Hong Kong law make travel easier for people crossing the border? (皇崗口岸港方區域由香港法律管轄，對跨境旅客有何幫助？)
lv3: Some people argue that deeper integration between Hong Kong and mainland China benefits the economy, while others worry it may blur the differences between the two systems. What do you think are the benefits and risks of arrangements like this one at Huanggang Port? (有人認為香港與內地加深融合有利經濟，但也有人擔心這會模糊「兩制」的分別。你認為皇崗口岸這類安排有何利弊？)

As border crossings between Hong Kong and Shenzhen become more efficient, what impact might this have on people's daily lives, businesses, and Hong Kong's identity as a unique city? (隨著香港與深圳之間的過境越來越便捷，這對市民生活、商業活動及香港的獨特城市身份有何影響？)

articles.title: Japan's Kumamoto Earthquake Toll Rises to 34 as Heatwave Hits Disaster Zone
articles.summary: A powerful earthquake that struck Japan's Kumamoto region has now caused at least 34 deaths, making it a serious natural disaster. Rescue teams continue to search for survivors in affected areas. On top of the destruction left by the quake, the disaster zone is also experiencing extreme heat, with temperatures soaring to 35 degrees Celsius. To protect survivors sheltering in evacuation centres, authorities rushed 300 mobile air-conditioning units to the area as quickly as possible. Extreme heat after a major earthquake is especially dangerous because many displaced people have no access to cool shelter, clean water, or electricity. Experts warn that heatstroke poses an additional threat to survivors and rescue workers alike.

lv1: How many people have died as a result of the Kumamoto earthquake? (熊本地震至今造成多少人死亡？)
What did authorities send to the evacuation centres to help survivors cope with the hot weather? (當局向避難所運送什麼設備，幫助災民應對酷熱天氣？)
lv2: Why is extreme heat especially dangerous for people living in evacuation centres after an earthquake? (為何地震後在避難所居住的人，面對酷熱天氣特別危險？)
What kinds of challenges do rescue workers face when they have to operate in both earthquake damage zones and extreme heat at the same time? (救援人員同時在地震災區和極端高溫環境下工作，會面對哪些挑戰？)
lv3: Japan is one of the world's most earthquake-prepared countries, yet disasters still cause significant loss of life. Do you think governments around the world invest enough in disaster preparedness and early warning systems? Use evidence to support your view. (日本是全球最具備地震防備的國家之一，但災難仍造成大量傷亡。你認為世界各地政府在災難應對和預警系統上的投資是否足夠？請以事實支持你的觀點。)

Climate change is making heatwaves more frequent and severe. How should disaster management plans be updated to account for the increasing overlap between natural disasters and extreme weather events? (氣候變化令熱浪更頻繁和嚴峻。防災計劃應如何更新，以應對自然災害與極端天氣事件日益重疊的情況？)

articles.title: 考評局公布2027年DSE考試費用　較今年輕微上調
articles.summary: 香港考試及評核局於7月31日公布2027年度中學文憑試（DSE）的各科報名費及自修生費用，新收費較2026年度有所上調。DSE是香港學生升讀大學的重要考試，每年均有大批中六學生及自修生報考。費用調整消息引起不少家長和學生關注，部分人擔心報考費用持續增加，會令經濟有困難的家庭更難負擔。考評局表示，調整費用是為了維持考試的質素及營運需要。學生如有財政困難，可向學校或有關部門申請費用資助。

lv1: 考評局公布的是哪一年度DSE考試的費用？
DSE考試對香港學生有什麼重要性？
lv2: 為什麼考試費用上調會令部分家庭感到擔憂？這反映了社會上什麼問題？
考評局指調整費用是為了維持考試質素，你認為考試費用與考試質素之間有什麼關係？
lv3: 有人認為公開考試費用不斷上升，對基層學生不公平，政府應全面資助所有學生的DSE費用；但也有人認為資源有限，資助應只針對有需要的學生。你支持哪種做法？為什麼？
香港的大學入學制度主要依賴DSE成績，這樣的制度是否公平？是否存在其他更好的方式評估學生的能力和潛力？

articles.title: 香港快運8月1日起上調燃油附加費　飛日韓泰航線加幅較大
articles.summary: 香港低成本航空公司香港快運宣布，由2026年8月1日起上調部分航線的燃油附加費。據報道，香港飛往內地航線的燃油附加費增至每程約198港元，而飛往日本、韓國及泰國等亞洲熱門旅遊目的地的附加費則增至約339港元。燃油附加費是機票費用以外另行收取的額外費用，主要用於應對航空燃油價格的變動。旅客在購買機票時須留意此項費用，以免低估旅遊總開支。有旅遊業界人士指出，收費上調或會影響部分旅客的出行計劃。

lv1: 香港快運從何時起上調燃油附加費？
燃油附加費是什麼？為什麼航空公司需要收取這項費用？
lv2: 為什麼飛往日本、韓國及泰國的燃油附加費，比飛往內地的附加費更高？
燃油附加費上調對不同類型的旅客（例如學生、家庭、商務旅客）可能有什麼不同的影響？
lv3: 航空公司將燃油成本轉嫁給乘客，是否合理的商業做法？政府應否規管航空附加費的上限，以保障消費者權益？
航空業是全球碳排放的重要來源之一。燃油價格上升雖令機票變貴，卻可能減少人們乘坐飛機的次數，從而有助環保。你認為這是減少航空業碳排放的有效方法嗎？還是有更好的解決方案？
